_comment: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE INSTALLER, FETCHED LIVE.
Everything the flasher needs to know that can change without the code
changing lives here: which images to offer, their checksums, which
hardware has actually been tested, where dependencies come from, the tier
thresholds, and every link the app shows a human.
WHY. A downloaded binary is frozen the day it is built. When an image is
reissued, a checksum rotates, a dependency moves or a board is finally
tested, a hardcoded binary is wrong until every user downloads a new one —
and most never will. Fetching this at startup means the app corrects
itself; the binary only carries a fallback copy for offline use.
os-list/sambuca-os-list.json is GENERATED from this file, so the image
facts exist in exactly one place. Do not hand-edit that file.

HOSTING IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, AND NOTHING HERE IS UNCACHED. raw.githubusercontent.com serves .json as text/plain, and rpi-imager ignores a list served that way - the device picker comes up empty with no error, which looks exactly like a broken list. Measured 2026-08-20: official=application/json, raw.github=text/plain, jsDelivr=application/json. So the OS LIST goes through jsDelivr. The manifest itself stays on raw because content-type does not matter to a Python client. BOTH ARE CACHED: raw sends Cache-Control max-age=300, so an edit takes up to ~5 minutes to appear, and jsDelivr holds a branch ref far longer. An earlier version of this note claimed raw was uncached and updated immediately; that was wrong, measured wrong, and would have had someone debugging a stale file as if it were a bad edit.

rpi_imager.reason: Writes the card. Sambuca does not implement image writing; this tool does it correctly on all three platforms and handles elevation itself.

images.name: Sambuca - Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit)

images.verified: extract_sha256 measured locally on 2026-08-20 by decompressing the verified download and hashing it; it matches the digest produced by a real write to a card.

tiers._comment: Mirrors engine/hardware-detect.sh. Served live so a threshold can be corrected without reissuing binaries. The ENGINE on the target machine remains authoritative; these values are what the estimator shows before you commit hardware.
